14.0.0.en: "Let not your heart be troubled": the discourse in the previous chapter was disturbing and frightening to the disciples, for it spoke of betrayal, death and denial, and because of all this their state of mind worsened.

14.0.1.en: Therefore Christ began to comfort and encourage them with kind words to remove their distress from them, and to offer them a remedy: faith in Him and in all that He had said, and that their faith in Him should be no less than their faith in God Himself. "Ye believe in God": here the Lord Christ gives the first beneficial remedy for anxiety and distress, which is offered to all of us and not only to the disciples. It is faith in God, that is, in Him, and in all His true promises that He promised us in the person of His disciples.

14.0.2.en: Faith in God, the powerful Ruler of all things who loves His children, is the first and most important remedy for anxiety; may we take refuge in Him in times of affliction and temptation.

14.1.0.en: Christ presents a bright side to His disciples: if He is parted from them for a while, it is for their sake and for ours, to prepare a place in heaven, where the glory is unseen. The words "many mansions" mean the infinite vastness of heaven, and also mean that there is one rank higher than another, as St. Paul indicated in (1 Cor 15:41). For if God, in His love, receives His believing children into His Kingdom, He also, in His justice, rewards each person according to his labor and striving.

14.2.0.en: My separation from you is not eternal, but I will come again, in My glory, and receive you unto Myself, and you will enjoy being with Me forever, after which there is no separation: "that where I am, there ye may be also."

14.2.1.en: This promise made the saints, in every generation, take no interest in this earthly life; rather, all their hearts were fixed on the bosom of Christ, for there is no feeling in the whole world that equals this spiritual feeling in its happiness.

14.3.0.en: "And whither I go ye know": what is meant is going to heaven, but passing through the way of the Cross.

14.4.s.en: (2) I am the way ... I am in the Father

14.4.0.en: It seems that what the Lord Christ said in the preceding verses did not satisfy Thomas, the rational disciple, but perhaps increased his perplexity, so we find him in a state of inquiry. He admitted that he did not know the place, and consequently did not know the way to it, and he phrased his question in a form in which he included the disciples with him.

14.5.0.en: As usual, the Lord Christ answers a limited question about time and place with a deep spiritual answer. He is the Way for everyone who is lost in the estrangement of the world and stumbling in his sins; and He is the Truth, that is, everything other than Him and outside faith in Him is falsehood; and He is the Life, so that whoever lives with Him on earth enjoys Him and is not troubled by the changes of the world, until he reaches Him in heaven, for He is eternal life, and "neither is there salvation in any other" (Acts 4:12). May we learn from Thomas to ask God and our guides in the Lord about everything we do not know, and God will reveal to us what is farther and deeper than our minds would have reached.

14.6.0.en: Here Christ links the disciples' knowledge of Him with the knowledge of the Father Himself, for the two are one in essence, and seeing the Son in His authority, His miracles and His commandment is seeing the essence of God Himself. Because the discourse was difficult, Philip did not understand Christ's intent, especially the word "ye have seen him," so he asked to see the Father plainly, if that was within Christ's power, forgetting what Christ had declared earlier: "I and my Father are one" (ch. 10:30). So the answer of the Lord Christ comes as a reproach ... After all these years and miracles and works and parables, have you still not known Me, Philip? For "he that hath seen me hath seen the Father."

14.6.1.en: This verse is considered a direct and clear declaration, added to the earlier declarations about the divinity of Christ, and St. John was careful to record it.

14.7.0.en: The Lord Christ continues His talk with Philip with a question, in which He invites him to examine himself as to the extent of his faith in Him, after having reproached him in (v. 9); then He turns His words to the rest of the disciples, declaring clearly that He is in the Father and the Father in Him. Here Christ affirms His equality with the Father, and that all the works He does have the Father as their source. To bring this truth nearer to our minds, we say that the relationship between the Father and the Son is like the relationship between the mind and thought: thought has its source in the mind, and the essence of the mind is thought, so there is no mind without thought and no thought without mind.

14.8.0.en: The discourse is still directed to the disciples, that they must believe that Christ is God, just as the Father is God. Because Christ knows that the time of the disciples' perfect faith had not yet come, He gives them proof of His oneness with the Father, which is the multitude of miracles and works that He did, which no one can do but God.

14.9.0.en: A precious, valuable and very encouraging promise to the holy disciples, and after them to everyone who has sincere faith in the Lord Christ, that he will do the very works of Christ, but through Christ Himself; for we have no power in ourselves, but it is His power given to us by the Holy Spirit (Acts 1:8).

14.9.1.en: "Greater works than these shall he do": it is impossible for a creature to do works greater than his Creator. But what Christ means here is that spiritual miracles, such as satisfying souls with the word of God, are greater than satisfying them with bread and fish, and giving life to souls dead in their sins by calling them to repentance is better than raising the dead bodily. Therefore, beloved, do not belittle what Christ can do through us, His Church, for He has deposited in her all His power, not for boasting, but for the salvation of others and the glorification of His holy name.

14.10.0.en: Here the Lord Christ presents the honor of His holy name, and the effectiveness and intercession of using this name in answering all who ask with faith ... The word "whatsoever" means the breadth of the circle of requests from the believing disciples, and the infinite power of using the name of Christ in answering. This is what made our Church, guided by the Holy Spirit, use the name of the Lord in all her prayers: she concludes the Lord's Prayer with the name of Christ Jesus our Lord, and repeats His holy name in all her praises and prayers.

14.10.1.en: 3) The promise of the Holy Spirit (vv. 15-26):

14.10.2.en: 15- If ye love me, keep my commandments. 16- And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; 17- Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you. 18- I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.

14.10.3.en: 19- Yet a little while, and the world seeth me no more; but ye see me: because I live, ye shall live also. 20- At that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you. 21- He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me: and he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him. 22- Judas saith unto him, not Iscariot, Lord, how is it that thou wilt manifest thyself unto us, and not unto the world? 23- Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him. 24- He that loveth me not keepeth not my sayings: and the word which ye hear is not mine, but the Father's which sent me. 25- These things have I spoken unto you, being yet present with you.

14.10.4.en: 26- But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.

14.11.0.en: True love for Christ is not an emotional feeling, but obedience, commitment and action according to His commandments; perfect obedience and faith are the sign of love and its proof.

14.12.0.en: "I will pray the Father": that is, after the completion of redemption and My ascension, as though the hypostasis of the Son hands over to the hypostasis of the Holy Spirit the care of the Church in her new covenant, which the Son began with His blood.

14.12.1.en: "Comforter": in Greek it means "comforter, helper, intercessor and advocate," and the Arabic translation has lost its meanings. These meanings give a quick glimpse of the work of the Holy Spirit in our lives, and in the Church in general.

14.12.2.en: "That he may abide with you for ever": that is, the words are not limited to the Church in the age of the Apostles only, but He is at work in her and in the life of her children until the end of the ages ... This verse is one of those in which the Holy Trinity meets: the Son asks, the Father answers, and the Holy Spirit is sent, because the will in the divine essence is one.

14.13.0.en: "The Spirit of truth": God is absolute truth. Therefore, whoever has not been born of this Spirit in Baptism cannot receive Him, for the world is material and sensual and sunk in falsehood; therefore it does not receive God, who is Spirit and Truth, and does not know Him. But whoever knows the Holy Spirit and makes Him dwell in his heart is the one who enjoys the true knowledge of God. "With you ... in you": the Holy Spirit no longer merely surrounds the children of God, but dwells within them, and this is a gift that each one of us received in the anointing with the Holy Myron; and this is what St. Paul reminds us of when he says: "What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you?" (1 Cor 6:19).

14.14.0.en: Since the hour of separation by death was near, Christ wanted to reassure His disciples that He would not leave them orphans after His death, but would come to them and they would see Him; this is, on the one hand, a direct reference to His appearing to His disciples for forty days after the Resurrection, and on the other hand, He speaks of the sending of the Holy Spirit and His permanent presence in them and with them, by which the person of Christ would always be revealed in them, by reminding them of all that He taught them and all that He commanded them. Consequently, they would not be orphans, so long as the Holy Spirit dwelt within them and with them.

14.15.0.en: "At that day": it carries two meanings: either after the declaration of His Resurrection, or the day of the descent of the Holy Spirit. And the word "ye shall know" here means you will be certain without any doubt. For despite the many earlier declarations of His oneness with the Father, the speech was obscure and not understood. But the day would come of complete certainty and the completion of the incomplete knowledge, either through His talks with them during the 40 days after His resurrection from the dead, or through the Holy Spirit, who would teach them mysteries that cannot be uttered.

14.16.0.en: This verse adds to what came in (v. 15) that there is a divine reward, which the hearts of the children of God who love Him and act by His commandments take hold of and enjoy, which is God's revealing Himself in their lives, so that they enjoy His presence and friendship more than others do; for God loves all people by calling them, but whoever acts by His commandments has another standing, for he sees God every day in his life.

14.17.0.en: "Judas": he is Thaddeus, the brother of James the son of Alphaeus, and the writer of the Epistle of Jude. He did not understand the Lord's intent here, for he thought that Christ would manifest Himself to the disciples only, without others seeing Him. This is what made him ask in wonder ... So Christ answered him again with what He had said before about the connection of our love for God with our acting by His commandments, and added and made clearer the recompense for that: that He and His Father would have presence and permanent dwelling, by the Holy Spirit, in the hearts of His children who act by His commandments, and this is a gift that surpasses all the gifts the spiritual man could wish for; it is not hosting for a temporary visit, but residence, companionship, friendship and permanent presence. Does this not encourage us, my friend, to put aside our excuses and laziness, and to strive to bring the commandment of Christ into the field of practice and struggle in it, so that we may enjoy seeing the hand of God working in our lives with a power that is tangible and perceived? And Christ attributes the words He spoke to the Father, to make clear the divine authority in these words, and also to affirm that He is the only Son who has declared Him (ch. 1:18).

14.18.0.en: That is, as though He were depositing His words in trust in their hearts before His departure from the world.

14.19.0.en: This is a return to what the Lord Christ began and spoke about concerning the Holy Spirit in (v. 16), and He makes clear His role with the disciples and the Church in all her generations ... He teaches us and guides us to the way of our salvation, and He is the One who always reminds us and brings to our minds all the words and teachings of the Lord Christ, and even urges us to carry them out and live by them in the midst of the world, and gives us the power needed for that.

14.20.0.en: Although the discourse here is directed to the disciples, it goes beyond them to the whole Church in every time and place. The inheritance of fathers to their children may be money or standing, but the inheritance of Christ and His gift is a peace that passes understanding and that the world does not understand, for the whole world cannot give any of this peace; and Christ's granting this peace as a gift from Him is a clear indication of His divinity, as Isaiah prophesied about Him: "And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace" (Isa 9:6).

14.20.1.en: The natural result of this peace is steadfastness of the heart and its fearlessness, whatever the terrors. Perhaps the most brilliant proof of this is the state of our fathers the martyrs at the time of their torments, for their peace and calm were bewildering and incomprehensible to those who were tormenting them.

14.21.0.en: "If ye loved me": ... that is, spiritual love and not emotional love, for emotion grieves at parting, but spiritual love goes beyond it, because it understands and is aware of the results of what happens after Christ's bodily separation from the disciples, such as: the preparation of the place (v. 2), the sending of the Holy Spirit (v. 16), and the permanent enjoyment with the Father and the Son, whether on earth (v. 23) or afterward in heaven (v. 3). Perhaps we also feel and understand this in our lives when one of our beloved saints departs to heaven: we miss him with human emotion, but in the Spirit we rejoice, since he has become an intercessor for us, asking on our behalf before the throne of grace, until we meet him there too.

14.21.1.en: "My Father is greater than I": ... not in nature, for the two are equal in essence. But He speaks of the glory of His divinity that was hidden during the journey of suffering and crucifixion, while the glory of the Father is not hidden, for the visible image of the Son in the coming days would be empty of all greatness in the human sense. Here St. Paul says of Christ: "made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant" (Phil 2:7), that is, He left aside showing His divine glory, in order to redeem mankind by His body. Since this verse is one of those that many heretics (dissenters and innovators) used to diminish the equality of the Son with the Father, here, beloved, is what Christ also said in the same Gospel on this matter:

14.21.2.en: 1) "My Father worketh hitherto, and I work" (ch. 5:17).

14.21.3.en: 2) "That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father" (ch. 5:23).

14.21.5.en: 4) "He that hath seen me hath seen the Father" (v. 9).

14.21.6.en: 5) "I am in the Father, and the Father in me" (v. 10).

14.21.7.en: 6) "And all mine are thine, and thine are mine" (ch. 17:10).

14.21.8.en: 7) "Thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee" (ch. 17:21).

14.22.0.en: That is, everything connected with the sufferings, the journey of the Cross and the hard times; so when they come, you will remember that I prophesied all this to you, and your faith will not faint but will be steadfast and increase.

14.22.1.en: Beloved, how much we need to remember the promises and words of the Lord Christ about His comforts, and His care for us in hard times. The more we have faith and hold fast to His presence, the more steadfastness and peace we receive in the midst of tribulations.

14.23.0.en: "Hereafter I will not talk much with you": that is, only a few hours remained for the disciples with Christ, the time of talking and teaching had passed, and only the time of redemption and the Cross remained.

14.23.1.en: "The prince of this world": this is the last war that Satan was about to wage ... the stirring up of the priests and the people, the carrying out of Judas' betrayal, and all the accompanying trials and conspiracies, and this is what Christ declared in (Lk 22:53): "this is your hour, and the power of darkness."

14.23.2.en: "And hath nothing in me": that is, Satan, with all his power, has no authority before the righteousness, greatness and authority of Christ.

14.23.3.en: And also, my beloved ... this same authority was given to the children of God. Satan is skilled at conspiracies and causes many outward wars, but he cannot triumph over any of the children of God, who alone have the authority to crush him, if they do not surrender to their passions and the evil desires of the world around them.

14.24.0.en: This verse is connected to the one before it: that although the prince of this world has nothing in Me, yet because I love the Father, I lay down My life according to His will for the salvation of the world.

14.24.1.en: Chapter fifteen: Christ likens Himself to the vine, and commands His disciples to love, and not to be disturbed by the world's opposition to Him and to them
